clinician.trajectory_summary: A 37-year-old Caucasian female nonsmoker with no known past medical history presented with 4 months of dyspnea and back pain. She had been initially misdiagnosed with pneumonia at an outside facility based on chest imaging showing right upper lobe consolidation. On admission to our facility, chest CT with IV contrast revealed near-complete right upper lobe collapse, right upper lobe consolidation, and enlarged subcarinal and station 6 lymph nodes. Abdominal CT identified a single 15-mm hypodense liver nodule. A fluoroscopy-guided liver biopsy was performed, which demonstrated a malignant undifferentiated neoplasm with epithelioid morphology and weak neuroendocrine differentiation. Histologically, the tumor cells formed nests and cords in a background of hyalinized sclerotic stroma, with eosinophilic cytoplasm and round-to-ovoid nuclei. Immunohistochemical staining revealed MUC4 expression with preserved BRG1 and INI1 nuclear staining, while claudin-4, ERG, CD31, CAMTA1, P40, ETV-4, and NUT stains were negative. Next-generation sequencing identified a WRN gene variant of unknown significance. Based on the constellation of histological features (epithelioid morphology, sclerotic stroma, nesting growth pattern), immunophenotype (MUC4 positive, preserved BRG1/INI1, negative claudin-4/ERG/CD31/CAMTA1/P40/ETV-4/NUT), and clinical presentation, a diagnosis of sclerosing epithelioid fibrosarcoma was concluded.

final.trajectory_summary: A 37-year-old Caucasian female nonsmoker with no known past medical history presented with 4 months of dyspnea and back pain. She had been initially misdiagnosed with pneumonia at an outside facility based on chest imaging showing right upper lobe consolidation. On admission to our facility, chest CT with IV contrast revealed near-complete right upper lobe collapse, right upper lobe consolidation, and enlarged subcarinal and station 6 lymph nodes. Abdominal CT identified a single 15-mm hypodense liver nodule. A fluoroscopy-guided liver biopsy was performed, which demonstrated a malignant undifferentiated neoplasm with epithelioid morphology and weak neuroendocrine differentiation. Histologically, the tumor cells formed nests and cords in a background of hyalinized sclerotic stroma, with eosinophilic cytoplasm and round-to-ovoid nuclei. Immunohistochemical staining revealed MUC4 expression with preserved BRG1 and INI1 nuclear staining, while claudin-4, ERG, CD31, CAMTA1, P40, ETV-4, and NUT stains were negative. Next-generation sequencing identified a WRN gene variant of unknown significance. Based on the constellation of histological features (epithelioid morphology, sclerotic stroma, nesting growth pattern), immunophenotype (MUC4 positive, preserved BRG1/INI1, negative claudin-4/ERG/CD31/CAMTA1/P40/ETV-4/NUT), and clinical presentation, a diagnosis of sclerosing epithelioid fibrosarcoma was concluded.
